# Dansk Psykiatrisk Selskab

Dansk Psykiatrisk Selskab is a Danish professional society (fagselskab) named as a represented body in the steering group ("styregruppen") of the ADHD-databasen, a Danish health quality database that monitors the assessment and treatment of ADHD in children and young people under 18 [^src1][^src2]. The organization appears twice in the corpus, both times simply listed as a member of this steering group, alongside overlæger, speciallæger, psykologer, sygeplejersker, epidemiologer and pårørenderepræsentanter from across Denmark [^src1][^src2].

The first mention, on page 41 of the 2023 ADHD documentation, sits within a section detailing the database's steering group membership and statistical data on children and young people assessed or treated for ADHD between 1 April 2023 and 31 March 2024, broken down by age group, sex and region; that document also reports that children and young people with ADHD have a markedly lower rate of passing the folkeskole leaving exam before age 17 compared with the general population [^src1]. The second mention, on page 61 of the 2024 documentation, appears in a similar steering-group listing, this time describing membership drawn from all five Danish regions, professional societies (fagselskaber), patient organizations, and Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut, accompanying appendices on ADHD assessment and treatment activity for the period 1 April 2024 – 31 March 2025 and on regional variation in the use of a course marker for "afkræftede mistanker" (disproven suspicions) [^src2].

No relationships, claims, or timeline events tied specifically to Dansk Psykiatrisk Selskab are recorded in the corpus beyond its listed presence in the steering group. Its significance rests on that role: it is one of the professional bodies represented in governing the ADHD-databasen's quality-monitoring work.
